dedupe_keys.name: austrian hail hazard map hailstone size return levels and return periods on a 1 km grid from 14 years of calibrated hail data

description: The Austrian hail hazard map gives, for every square kilometre of Austria, how large hailstones are expected to be for given return periods and how often a given size recurs. The Zenodo record read on 2026-09-28, published in July 2025 by Gregor Ehrensperger of the University of Innsbruck and Marc-André Falkensteiner, explains that return levels and periods were estimated with a spatio-temporal metastatistical approach from 14 years of calibrated hailstone size data of GeoSphere Austria, and are provided in a single CSV file of about 26 MB on a 1 km grid, with a README and an accompanying manuscript on arXiv. Coverage is Austria. The data are free under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and users are asked to cite the manuscript. Caveats: a 14-year record is short for rare events, and the column layout was not inspected. It supports hazard exposure and adaptation studies, such as estimating hail damage to roofs, photovoltaic plants, vehicles or greenhouses and choosing hail-resistant design levels by region. Related records: the Austrian HORA natural hazard portal and a global daily large hail probability dataset.
name: Austrian hail hazard map: hailstone size return levels and return periods on a 1 km grid from 14 years of calibrated hail data
